scope: Multiple learned technical completions sharing prefix; frequency versus recency
finding: Core can return three matches but application requests default one and takes first; frequency dominates recency until counts tie.
evidence: Old address used 20 times remains sole default offer after recent address has been used 19 times.
At equal count 20, most recent wins in all three families.
Typing discriminating prefix yields desired address in all three controls.
classification: Typing-convenience opportunity; implementation matches current frequency-first single-offer design, not a proven correctness violation.
proposal: Expose several matching saved addresses for direct choice; separately evaluate recency-sensitive ranking rather than assuming most recent always desired.
limits: Core recall observations plus inspected application single-slot routing; not live UI.
No claim new address is never learned or inaccessible; longer prefix works.
No automatic edit or forced selection.
